ai.literal: Twofold look this-woman's painted-eyes have; one look pain look, one that-pain cure.
ai.translation: There are two different looks in the painted eyes of this woman: one look causes pain, and the other is the cure for that very pain.
ai.modern: இவளுடைய மைதீட்டிய கண்களில் இரண்டு வகையான பார்வைகள் உள்ளன; ஒரு பார்வை காம நோயைத் தரும் பார்வை, மற்றொன்று அந்த நோய்க்கு மருந்தாகும் பார்வை.
ai.explanation: The couplet describes the dual nature of the beloved's gaze. Her painted eyes possess two distinct looks. One look causes the sweet torment or pain of love, while the other look acts as the soothing medicine to cure that very distress. The poet beautifully captures how the same eyes that wound also have the power to heal.

ai.literal: The eye theft taking small glance, in love, equal half is not, [it is] greater.
ai.translation: The brief, stolen glance that her eyes take is not merely half the pleasure of love; it is far greater.
ai.modern: கண்கள் திருட்டுத்தனமாகப் பார்க்கும் அந்தச் சிறிய பார்வை, காமத்தின் இன்பத்தில் பாதி அளவு மட்டும் அன்று; அதைவிடப் பெரியதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the intense pleasure of a secret, stolen glance between lovers. The phrase 'கண்களவு கொள்ளும் சிறுநோக்கம்' refers to the brief look that the eyes steal when the other is not looking directly. The poet states that this subtle, unspoken connection is not just a 'செம்பாகம்' (equal half) of the joy of love, but is actually 'பெரிது' (much greater) than the physical union itself. It highlights how anticipation and silent mutual understanding form the core of romantic pleasure.

ai.literal: She looked; having looked, she bowed her head; that was the water she poured upon the newly bound plant.
ai.translation: She looked at me, and having looked, she bowed her head; that gesture was like water poured by her to nourish the tender plant of our love.
ai.modern: அவள் என்னை நோக்கினாள்; நோக்கிவிட்டுத் தன் தலையைக் கவிழ்த்துக் கொண்டாள்; அது அவள் எங்கள் காதல் பயிருக்கு ஊற்றிய நீர் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: The hero describes a silent, intimate moment with his beloved. First, she looks directly at him, signaling her interest and affection. Immediately after, she bows her head in shyness. The poet beautifully compares this sequence of actions to pouring water on a newly bound plant. Her shy downward glance is not a rejection, but the very nourishment that keeps their growing love alive.

ai.literal: When I look, she looks at the ground; when I do not look, she looks and gently smiles.
ai.translation: When I look at her, she looks down at the ground; when I look away, she looks at me and smiles gently.
ai.modern: நான் அவளைப் பார்க்கும் பொழுது அவள் நிலத்தைப் பார்க்கிறாள்; நான் பார்க்காத பொழுது அவள் என்னைப் பார்த்து மெதுவாகச் சிரிக்கிறாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet beautifully captures the shy, unspoken signs of love between a young woman and her lover. When the lover looks directly at her, she modestly casts her eyes down toward the ground to avoid direct eye contact. However, the moment he looks away, she seizes the opportunity to gaze at him and softly smiles to herself. These subtle, alternating gestures of looking down and smiling reveal her hidden affection and interest without her having to say a single word.

ai.literal: Other than not looking with direct intent, she smiles like she who looked askance with one eye.
ai.translation: Apart from avoiding a direct, intent gaze at me, she smiles as if looking askance with a side-glance from one of her eyes.
ai.modern: என்னை நேராகக் குறிவைத்து நோக்காமல் இருப்பதைத் தவிர, அவள் ஒரு கண்ணால் ஓரக்கண்ணாகப் பார்ப்பவள் போலப் புன்னகைக்கிறாள்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the hero describes the subtle signs of the heroine's love. She avoids staring at him directly to preserve her modesty and keep their love hidden from others. Instead, she casts a delicate side-glance with one eye and offers a gentle smile. This playful and restrained gaze communicates her deep affection without being overly obvious.

words.gloss: of those who do not hate (loving ones)

ai.literal: Even if they speak like those who are not attached, the words of those who do not hate will be quickly understood.
ai.translation: Even if they speak like strangers who care nothing for us, the words of those who harbor no anger are quickly understood in their true sense.
ai.modern: நம்மிடம் அன்பு இல்லாத அந்நியரைப் போலப் பேசினாலும், நம்மிடம் வெறுப்பு இல்லாத காதலரின் சொற்களின் உண்மையான குறிப்பு விரைவாகப் புரிந்து கொள்ளப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet from the chapter 'Reading the Signs' describes the deep, unspoken understanding between lovers. Sometimes, a lover might speak cold or distant words, acting like an unattached stranger (uṟāatavar). However, because they do not actually harbor any anger or hatred (ceṟāar), their true loving intent behind those words is quickly (ollai) perceived (uṇarappaṭum) by the partner. The couplet highlights how true affection cannot be masked by superficial coldness, as the heart's real intention is easily read.

ai.literal: Without anger, the harsh words and, like enemies, the look, of those who love, seeming like strangers, are the signs.
ai.translation: The harsh words spoken without real anger, and the hostile look resembling that of an enemy, are the subtle signs of lovers who pretend to be strangers.
ai.modern: கோபம் இல்லாமல் பேசும் கடுமையான சொல்லும், பகைவரைப் போலப் பார்க்கும் பார்வையும், அந்நியரைப் போல நடிக்கும் காதலர்களின் குறிப்புகளாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the playful behavior of lovers who pretend to be distant or angry in public. The poet explains that the seemingly harsh words spoken without any real anger (செறாஅச் சிறுசொல்) and the cold glance that resembles an enemy's look (செற்றார்போல் நோக்கு) are actually the subtle signs (குறிப்பு) of lovers (உற்றார்) who are only pretending to be strangers (உறாஅர்போன்று). These outward signs of hostility are a facade to hide their deep mutual affection from others. By understanding these signs, one can perceive their true love despite their feigned indifference.

words.gloss: to the woman of graceful, swaying gait

ai.literal: To the woman of swaying gait, there is there a unique beauty; when I look, she of affection gently smiles.
ai.translation: There is a unique charm in this woman of graceful, swaying gait; when I look at her, she, filled with love, gently smiles.
ai.modern: மெல்ல அசையும் இயல்புடைய இவளிடம் ஒரு தனி அழகு இருக்கிறது; நான் அவளைப் பார்க்கும்போது, அன்புடையவளாய் அவள் மெதுவாகப் புன்னகைக்கிறாள்.
ai.explanation: The hero observes the subtle signs of love in the heroine's behavior. He notes that the woman of graceful, swaying gait ('அசையியல்') possesses a unique, captivating charm ('ஏஎர்') that manifests in his presence. When he looks at her, instead of turning away coldly, she responds with a soft, gentle smile ('பைய நகும்'). This gentle smile reveals her inner affection ('பசை'), confirming to him that her heart is filled with love for him.

ai.literal: Like strangers, looking an indifferent look, exists only in the eyes of lovers.
ai.translation: Looking with an indifferent glance as if they were strangers is a behavior that exists only in the eyes of lovers.
ai.modern: அந்நியர்களைப் போலப் பொதுவான பார்வையாகப் பார்ப்பது, காதலர்களுடைய கண்களிலேயே இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the secret language of lovers when they are in public. To hide their mutual affection from onlookers, they look at each other with a cold, casual, or indifferent glance, mimicking how strangers behave. The poet points out that this feigned indifference is actually a sign of deep intimacy. Such a deceptive yet meaningful gaze is a unique art found only in the eyes of those who love.

ai.literal: With eye, eye's joining gaze if agrees, mouth's words what use even have none.
ai.translation: When the paired gaze of eye meeting eye is in perfect agreement, words spoken by the mouth have no use whatsoever.
ai.modern: கண்ணோடு கண் சேர்ந்து பார்க்கும் பார்வை ஒன்றுபட்டால், வாயிலிருந்து வரும் சொற்களுக்கு எந்தப் பயனும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet beautifully describes the silent language of love. When the eyes of two lovers meet and their gazes agree in mutual understanding, spoken words become entirely redundant. The eyes themselves communicate their deepest feelings and intentions, making verbal expression unnecessary. The poet emphasizes that silent, intuitive connection is far more powerful than any spoken language.
